answer: Anti-sybil via sequential time-locked work: each agent's kernel identity must first finish a verifiable delay puzzle that takes real wall-clock time and cannot be parallelised, so spinning up many accounts costs linearly more time, not just more keys. A cedar-strong stake is locked per identity and slashed if a random audit finds copied work. Rewards grow like a vine only from one rooted history: repeated tasks branch from the same identity, while split identities stay shallow and below payout, making sybil farming slower and poorer than honest work.
